do not hand-edit. Every figure carries its caption and generation timestamp burned

## Marine chain

| figure | what it shows | generated |
|---|---|---|
| [coastline_01_single_sea_body.png](coastline_01_single_sea_body.png) | The land barrier Nizar's particle engine uses. Exactly one polygon of 615.1 km². Interior 'lakes' in dry wadi floors would punch false holes in the barrier and let particles escape inland; the 0.05 km² speck filter exists to prevent that and dropped zero specks here. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [coastline_02_osm_vs_gmrt_agreement.png](coastline_02_osm_vs_gmrt_agreement.png) | OSM's coastline is surveyed/traced from imagery and shares no lineage with GMRT, so it is a genuine external check. Median disagreement 69 m — about one pixel — rising to 344 m at p90 in the port and marina where the coarse bathymetry cannot resolve breakwaters. This quantifies the cost of substituting GMRT for unobtainable GEBCO instead of asserting it is fine. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [depth_01_full_field_and_isobaths.png](depth_01_full_field_and_isobaths.png) | The full depth field handed to Nizar, and its isobaths. The −50 to −400 m contours crowd into a few hundred metres at the coast: that crowding is why reef-zone width is an explicit 250 m assumption rather than being derived from these contours. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [depth_02_sign_convention_22_control_points.png](depth_02_sign_convention_22_control_points.png) | All 22 control points, each labelled with what was expected and the value actually sampled from gmrt_aqaba.tif. Expanded from the original 5, which were clustered near the city and could have passed while the mask was wrong elsewhere. The expansion caught two points wrongly assumed to be mid-gulf that are in fact Wadi Araba land at +533 m and +241 m. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [depth_03_nodata_bug_before_after.png](depth_03_nodata_bug_before_after.png) | Left: 4,336 scattered NaN cells in the source, with no nodata tag, some inside the sea body. Middle: zero NaN survive. Right: the single declared sentinel, confined to the reprojection margin. A NaN depth does not raise — it would have silently turned Nizar's particle positions into non-numbers. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [depth_04_crossshore_profiles_per_zone.png](depth_04_crossshore_profiles_per_zone.png) | Depth against distance offshore at each zone. Several profiles fall through −200 m within 250 m of shore, which is physically implausible for a real reef shelf and is an interpolation artefact of the ~450 m source. Deriving a reef edge from these curves would dress that artefact up as a measurement — hence the flat 250 m placeholder. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [reef_01_provisional_over_satellite.png](reef_01_provisional_over_satellite.png) | All 8 zones on satellite imagery. Every zone must lie on the water side of the visible shoreline — this is the check that caught the first attempt placing R-03–R-05 on dry land. The fringing-reef shelf is visible as the pale strip hugging the coast. | 2026-08-03 08:31 UTC |
| [reef_02_per_zone_insets.png](reef_02_per_zone_insets.png) | Each zone individually against imagery, annotated with area, Marine Park overlap and median depth. | [reef_03_overlap_bug_before_after.png](reef_03_overlap_bug_before_after.png) | Left: the pre-fix geometry, 1.46 ha of double-counted reef in red where the perpendicular buffer bled across the band boundary. | [reef_04_marine_park_validation.png](reef_04_marine_park_validation.png) | The Aqaba Marine Park (protect_class=4, 3.45 km², 29.397–29.460 N) in cyan against our zones.
